description: Erection of a three to five storey block of flats containing 66 self-contained units (Class C3) (mix of 1, 2, 3 and 4 beds) with associated undercroft surfaced level car and bicycle parking, hard and soft landscaping, with all necessary ancillary and enabling works following the demolition of seven single storey vacant buildings (Sui Generis)
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - Time Limit

The development hereby permitted shall be begun within 3 years from the date of this permission.

Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92 (1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Condition : 2 - In accordance with approved drawings

The proposed development shall be carried out in all respects in accordance with the proposals contained in the application and the plans submitted [QDL04-MAA-01-XX-DG-A-003 Rev P01, QDL04-MAA-00-XXDG-A-004 Rev P02, QDL04-MAA-01-XX-DG-A-0001 Rev P03, Tree Survey, Arboricultural Impact Assessment and Arboricultural Method Statement, Air Quality Assessment, Acoustic Assessment, Design and Access Statement, Delivery and Servicing Plan, Health Impact Assessment, Heritage Statement, Fire Statement, RIBA Stage 2 Pre-Planning Fire Strategy, Landscape Design Report, Outline Construction Logistic Plan, Planning Statement, Preliminary Ecological Appraisal, RSPCA Letter, Statement of Community Involvement and Tree Protection Plan. Received 02/04/2024; Biodiversity Net Gain Metric. Received 04/04/2024; QDL04-MAA-00-XX-DG-A-0001 Rev P04. Received 30/04/2024; Design and Access Statement Addendum Visuals. Received 06/06/2024; Preliminary Risk Assessment and Intrusive Geo-environmental Investigation Report and Ground Investigation Letter. Received 21/06/2024; Statement of Community Involvement Addendum. Received 16/07/2024; Biodiversity Net Gain Report, Energy Statement, Flood Risk Assessment, Surface Water Exceedance Flow Routes, 1 in 30 Year Basin (Calculations), 1 in 30 Year Permeable Paving (Calculations), 1 in 30 Year Overflow Basin (Calculations), 1 in 100 Year + 40% Overflow Basin (Calculations), 1 in 100 Year +40% Overflow Basin (Calculations), 1 in 100 Year + 40% Overflow Basin (Calculations), 1 in 100 Year + 40% Permeable Paving (Calculations), 1 in 100 Year Basin (Calculations), 1 in 100 Year Overflow Basin (Calculations), 1 in 100 Year Permeable Paving (Calculations), Transport Statement and Travel Plan Statement. Received 04/02/2025; Design and Access Statement Addendum (Amenity, Overlooking and Privacy). Received 10/02/2025; Car Club Proposal, River Condition Assessment (RCA) - Photos, River Condition Assessment (RCA) - Summary

Condition : 5 - Carbon Energy Strategy

No development shall take place until the applicant has entered into a binding arrangement with the Council to make an agreed contribution to the Council's Carbon Offset Fund, in accordance with the zero carbon strategy set out in the Energy Statement hereby approved to an amount that equates to the shortfall in required energy savings to meet the 'zero carbon' target.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy and any subsequent approved revisions.

Upon final commencement of operation of any low and zero carbon technologies, performance data for energy consumption must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The performance data shall be submitted every 18 months to a monitoring web-platform for a period of three years from the point of full operation.

Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.

Condition : 6 - Water efficiency

Prior to first occupation of the building(s) hereby approved, the development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.

Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.

Condition : 7 - Sustainable sourcing of materials

The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of delivery notes, invoices or installation contracts) have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the development meets the following:

� At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification.

� At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.

� No construction or insulation materials are to be used which will release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone.

Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.

Condition : 8 - Screening

Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved plans and design and access statement, prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved, details to ensure privacy (e.g. through balcony screens, screening louvres or alternative fenestration treatment to balconies and windows) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.

Reason: To safeguard the amenity of future neighbouring occupiers and nearby residents'.

Condition : 10 - Inclusive Access Strategy

No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until an Inclusive Access Strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, which shall include: [details of the arrival, entrance and movement through the buildings ensuring a full automated solution, and how any level changes around the site would be overcome; and details of seating suitable for disabled carers].

The approved details shall be implemented fully before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use and shall be retained as such thereafter.

Reason: To provide a socially inclusive and sustainable development.

Condition : 12 - Cycle parking

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved full details (including manufacturers' specifications) of secure covered cycle parking facilities that accord with the West London Cycle Parking Guidance (for not less than 146 bicycles) for the occupants of the development and short-stay cycle parking facilities (for not less than 10 bicycles) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.

Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 13 - Delivery and Servicing Plan

Prior to first occupation of the development, an updated Delivery and Servicing Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by Transport for London and shall include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements, physical as well as managerial, for the servicing, including emergency vehicle access, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The plan shall include a management solution to ensure refuse bins are taken out for collection and returned to the bin stores after collection as well as details demonstrating where vehicles would stop for waste collection. 

The Plan shall be carried out as approved. The approved measures shall be implemented before the first occupation of the development hereby permitted and shall be so maintained for the life of the development.

Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives in accordance with adopted.

Condition : 14 - Car Parking Management Plan

Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include the following:

(i) details of parking allocations for residents of the approved development (including blue badge bays) and how this will be operated and enforced

(ii) details of measures proposed to restrict parking to designated bays only and prohibit parking on the access road

(iii) a commitment to convert passive EV bays to active when demand requires.

(iv) details of the operation of any gates or barriers

(v) measures to ensure that all prospective residents are informed of the Parking Management Plan and that all future residents will not be assigned a parking space or a right to park within the development other than blue badge holders.

The parking areas and access road(s) shall thereafter be managed in compliance with the approved Parking Management Plan, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to secure any variation.

Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure minimal disruption of traffic in the locality.

Condition : 15 - Waste storage

Prior to the first occupation of the hereby approved development the waste and recycling stores shall be made available for use in strict accordance with the approved plans and shall thereafter be retained as such, without obstruction, for the duration of the development.

Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling.

Condition : 16 - Land Quality - Remediation Method Statement / Remediation Strategy

Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:

If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety. 

Supporting Notes:

(i) The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.

(ii) The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority.

(iii) Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.

(iv) The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 17 - Land quality - additional/unexpected contamination found during development

During the development:

The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues. A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety. 

Supporting Notes:

(i) Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.

(ii) In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.

(iii) The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 18 - Land quality - verification and validation of remedial work

Prior to the development is first brought into use:

The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the local planning authority.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety. 

Supporting Notes:

(i) The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement.

(ii) This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.

(iii) The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 19 - Drainage Design

Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations [and updated Drainage Assessment Form] to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the Flood Risk Assessment (15/01/2025) and associated drawings. The options for discharge further up the hierarchy should be investigated including conducting infiltration testing and investigating the potential for discharge to the canal before proposing a connection to the foul sewer. Further information should be provided regarding the proposed rainwater harvesting feature. If rainwater harvesting is not proposed, the applicant should provide suitable justification for its non-inclusion. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be provided.

Reason: In order to prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site.

Condition : 20 - Built in Accordance with Drainage Details

No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.

Reason: To ensure that the methods to mitigate the risk of surface water flooding have been implemented as agreed and that the drainage system is suitably managed.

Condition : 21 - Bird Hazard Management Plan

Development shall not commence until a Bird Hazard Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted plan shall include details of:

- Management of any flat/shallow pitched/green roofs on buildings within the site which may be attractive to nesting, roosting and "loafing" birds. The management plan shall comply with Advice Note 3 'Wildlife Hazards around an Aerodrome'.

The Bird Hazard Management Plan shall be implemented as approved and shall remain in force for the life of the building. No subsequent alterations to the plan are to take place unless first submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: It is necessary to manage the flat roofs in order to minimise its attractiveness to birds which could endanger the safe movement of aircraft and the operation of Heathrow Airport.

Condition : 22 - Design Out Crime

Prior to occupation, the development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO).

No dwelling shall be occupied until accreditation has been achieved and evidence of such accreditation has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In pursuance of the Council's duty under section 17 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 to consider crime and disorder implications in excising its planning functions; to promote the well-being of the area in pursuance of the Council's powers under section 2 of the Local Government Act 2000 and to ensure the development provides a safe and secure environment in accordance with policy CC2 of the Local Plan (adopted 2015) and Policy D11 of the London Plan (adopted 2021) coupled with the requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework 2024.

Condition : 23 - Fixed Plant Noise Criteria

The cumulative noise from any fixed external plant associated with the scheme should not exceed levels more than 10 dB below representative background (LA90) levels at free field locations representing facades of nearby existing and proposed dwellings. Noise levels should be assessed by measurement or calculation based on the guidance presented within BS4142: 2014+A1:2019 or subsequent versions of this guidance.

Reason: In order to ensure that existing and proposed residential units are not exposed to unreasonable levels fixed plant noise.

Condition : 24 - Internal and External Noise Criteria

Maximum noise levels permitted within the dwellings will not exceed those that are specified in Table 4 of British Standard 8233:2014 [Living Rooms = 35 dB LAeq, 16 hours; Dining room/area = 40 dB LAeq, 16 hours; Bedroom = 35 dB LAeq, 16 hours during day-time (07:00 - 23:00) and Bedroom = 30 dB LAeq, 8 hours during night-time (23:00 - 07:00), night-time (23:00 � 07:00) LAmax noise levels within bedrooms do not exceed 45 dB LAmax more than 10 to 15 times per night. All occupiers should have access to amenity spaces where noise levels do not exceed 50dB LAeq,16hours.

Reason: In order to secure acceptable living conditions for residents of the new dwellings.

Condition : 25 - Construction Noise Limits

Based upon guidance contained within BS 5228:2009 + A1:2014: Noise, Noise levels from construction works at nearby existing and proposed residential receptors shall not exceed the following construction noise criteria:

� Daytime works will not exceed 75 dB LAeq,T at the worst-affected residential property during the following time periods:

� Monday to Friday (08:00 � 18:00 hours)

� Saturday (08:00 to 13:00 hours)

Works outside of the standard hours will be subject to prior agreement and prior notice will be provided to the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 26 - All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM)

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development hereby approved shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance (SPG) 'Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' dated July 2014, or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/.

The development shall also demonstrate that the proposed development is complaint with Building Emissions Benchmark (BEBs), specified in the GLA's Supplementary Planning Guidance "Sustainable Design and Construction" dated April 2014).

Reason: To minimise air pollution in the interests of air quality and the wider local environment.
